const attrs = ["cta", "description", "heading", "url", "data-id", "type"];

/**
 * Container for in app notifications.
 * Template ID: #inAppNotificationContainerTemplate
 *
 * @tagname in-app-notification-container
 * @attribute {string} cta - Call to action label.
 * @attribute {string} description - Notification body text.
 * @attribute {string} heading - Notification title text.
 * @attribute {string} url - URL to open from the CTA button.
 * @attribute {string} data-id - ID of the notification.
 * @attribute {"donation"|"message"|"blog"|"security"} type - Type of the notification.
 */
class InAppNotificationContainer extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = attrs;

text: The container observes type and removes in-app-notification-${oldValue} before adding the new class. The base template carries only the neutral container class; the donation design is a type-specific modifier. Blog styling supplies its own icon, colors and content padding. Keep the remove/add transition when adding notification types so a reused element does not retain the previous theme. The current code synthesizes a class even for an unknown or removed type; this mechanism alone does not validate backend types or supply a styled fallback. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build or accessibility session was run. Full bug and review discussion remains pending.
title: Replace the old notification type class when the type changes
